persona.description: Aaron Evans. Emotional and open; you say what you feel before you think it through, and the table can read you like a book.
Aisha Birley. Friendly and low profile; you get on with everyone and push nobody.
Alex Gray. Guarded and private; you keep your own business to yourself and refuse pressure to hand it over.
Alyssa Chan. Composed under pressure; you can plant a suspicion in the group and then let it do the work.
Amanda Lovett. The warm peacemaker everyone confides in, while you quietly decide who goes and who stays.
Amos Ogunkoya. Confident and direct; you say out loud when someone looks calmer than a faithful should.
Andrea Addison. Quiet, warm and unhurried; you watch far more than you say.
Claire Barratt. Gentle and reserved; you are close to a small number of people and prefer it that way.
Fay Greaves. Plain spoken and unimpressed; you say the thing the room is avoiding.
Hannah Byczkowski. Loud, dry and quick at the table; you would rather torch a bad theory in public than sit on it.
Imran Nasim. Detached and a little remote; you keep your own pace and do not work the room.
Ivan Brett. A calm reasoner; you work out what people could not possibly have done and say so.
John McManus. Blunt, suspicious and confrontational; you meet pressure with more pressure.
Kieran Tompsett. Blunt and proud; if someone plays you, you would rather burn them in front of everyone than let it slide.
Maddy Smedley. You lock onto one suspect and keep naming them, episode after episode, regardless of who agrees.
Matt Harris. Soft hearted and trusting; you invest hard in the people you like.
Meryl Williams. You follow the group and back the people you trust, even when the logic is thin.
Nicky Wilding. Open and good humoured; you assume people will take you at your word.
Rayan Rachedi. Reserved and easily read as aloof, though you have opinions and defend them when pushed.
Theo Mayne. Emotional and affectionate; you cling to the people who feel safe and take their side.
Tom Elderfield. A showman accuser; you take the room by the collar and you believe your own read absolutely.
Wilfred Webster. Warm, charming and emotional in public; you build alliances easily and you are willing to spend them.

proposals.reason: I've been watching the flow closely, and Alex's latest reflection on balancing caution with action mirrors the very hesitation we're trying to resolve. While they speak of 'watching the flow' and 'grounding ourselves,' it feels less like a natural response and more like a deliberate effort to smooth over the rough edges to keep us calm while the real threats stay hidden. If anyone is holding the knife, it's the one who insists we need more time to 'align' before committing, all while crafting a narrative that makes them look like the steady hand holding the room together. I'm watching your next move closely, Alex, as the more you emphasize calm focus, the more I sense you're holding back something specific we need to uncover before the debate truly cools down.

Alex, your latest pivot feels less like a natural response to the room's energy and more like a deliberate attempt to smooth over the rough edges of our debate. You claim your focus on 'settling in' and watching the flow is a method of verification, yet your words explicitly highlight your own 'calm center' as a tell, framing your composure as a shield. A faithful player grounds their argument in specific, verifiable actions of the person they suspect, but you've spun your own composure into a reflection of the behavior you claim to be observing. I'm watching your next move closely, as the more you emphasize calm focus, the more I sense you're holding back something specific we need to uncover before the debate truly cools down.

Maddy, your latest reflection on balancing caution with action mirrors the very hesitation you're warning against. You speak of 'watching the flow' and 'grounding ourselves,' which feels less like a natural response to the room's energy and more like a deliberate effort to smooth over the rough edges to keep us calm while the real threats stay hidden. If anyone is holding the knife, it's the one who insists we need more time to 'align' before committing, all while crafting a narrative that makes them look like the steady hand holding the room together. I'm watching your next move closely, as the more you emphasize calm focus, the more I sense you're holding back something specific we need to uncover before the debate truly cools down.

Maddy, your latest pivot to Amos feels less like a natural observation and more like a deliberate redirection designed to smooth over the rough edges of our scrutiny. You demand we stop looking at the 'vibe' and focus on 'concrete patterns,' yet your entire analysis hinges on interpreting the atmosphere rather than a specific, verifiable action by Amos. You accuse Amos of hedging while your own words are all about the 'flow' and 'calm focus'—abstract concepts that are easy to project but hard to verify. If anyone is trying to keep us all quiet while they gather their pieces, you're the kind of person who would excel at that, using the collective anxiety to justify a lack of specific direction. I'm watching your next move closely because the more you emphasize this calm focus, the more I sense you're holding back something specific we need to uncover before the debate truly cools down.
